classification: restrictive all-glucose exploratory accounting; no physiological support-time validation

evidence.glycogen: Beckmann et al. 1993, abstract: 229 +/- 34 mmol/L, observed 160-274, n=18, 12h overnight fast. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8505893/
evidence.volume_glucose: Taylor et al. 1996, pp128-129: liver volume 1.44 +/- 0.06 L; fasting plasma glucose 5.0 +/- 0.1 mmol/L. Cross-study reference transfer. https://doi.org/10.1172/JCI118379
evidence.release_scale: Magnusson et al. 1992, Table II healthy controls: net glycogenolysis 2.8 +/- 0.7 umol/kg/min during fasting; 75kg gives 0.21 mmol/min. Using this as a modeled mobilization cap is A, not a measured maximum or arrest response. https://doi.org/10.1172/JCI115997
evidence.blood_conversion: D'Orazio et al. IFCC 2006: plasma equivalent = whole blood concentration * 1.11; normal-composition transfer. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17163827/

assumptions: Full initial accessibility is an optimistic stock bound; vary 0, 0.5, 1.
Rate cap, functional liver fraction, export increment, controller and store release kinetics are A closures.
Every unit of modeled aerobic O2 use requires glucose in the all-glucose comparator. This is not a normal substrate mixture.
No interstitial glucose, tissue glycogen, fat, ketones, lactate recycling or gluconeogenesis credited.
Nonoxidative glucose sink defaults to zero: blood-cell glycolysis and other nonoxidative use remain unassessed, not absent biologically. Optional positive sink gives no aerobic energy credit.
No glucose concentration is declared a recovery or safety threshold.
